subject: Implementation timeline, feature-flag canaries, and telemetry handoff - Astra Financial
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@astra.com>
Cc: procurement@astra.com
Date: 2026-06-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation timeline, feature-flag canaries, and telemetry handoff - Astra Financial

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the RFI follow-up earlier. Attached is Redwood's implementation response tailored to the Astra Financial environment (Astra_RFI_Implementation_Response_v1.pdf). The doc includes a proposed phased activation timeline, expected integration touchpoints, and a short canary runbook. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm target production date window (you mentioned late Q3).
- Confirm which Astra environments we can access for e2e testing (staging, pre-prod, perf).
- Any compliance/approval gating beyond SOC2 and internal procurement?

Key highlights in the attachment:
- Phase 0 (Prework): network allowlist, KMS key exchange, test data subset provisioning (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (Integration): connector development + validation, schema handshake, basic auth flows (3 weeks)
- Phase 2 (Canary + Telemetry): feature-flagged canary at 1/5/25/50% over 2 weeks with telemetry baselines
- Phase 3 (Scale & Cutover): scaling ramp to sustained throughput and final SLA handoff (1 week)

I've copied our solutions lead Aditya and PM Karthik to add technical notes and telemetry specifics.

Next step: can we schedule a 30-min alignment call this week to lock the environment dates and sign-off on the canary gates?

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Astra_RFI_Implementation_Response_v1.pdf (summary + timeline)

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the PDF — useful level of detail. A few clarifying questions before we loop in our engineering leads:

1) For Phase 0, can you confirm which telemetry endpoints require access from our side? We prefer minimal egress for PII reasons.
2) The canary percentages look reasonable — can you briefly describe the automated rollback triggers you recommend?
3) Regarding KMS, do you support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for token encryption at rest?

Procurement dropped the high-level SOW terms in the cc; we'll need an estimate of elapsed engineering hours per phase to align on billing milestones.

Samantha
Head of Platform Integrations
Astra Financial

procurement@astra.com included for SOW cadence and billing questions.

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@astra.com
Date: 2026-06-25T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation timeline, feature-flag canaries, and telemetry handoff - Astra Financial

Hi Samantha — quick answers inline, then a short attachment that breaks down hours by phase.

1) Telemetry endpoints: minimal set is outlined in telemetry_schema.yaml attached. We only require:
   - anonymized request/response metadata (latency, model_id, token_count)
   - per-route error rate and 95th/99th latency metrics
   - optional sample of text payloads (configurable and redacted)
   We can consume metrics via a TLS-secured push to your datadog/hosted collector or pull via a secure webhook — your preference.

2) Rollback triggers (automated + manual):
   - Automated: >3x baseline error rate OR sustained 2x 95th percentile latency over 15 minutes -> auto-reduce canary to previous step and alert on-call.
   - Manual: product/infra can flip feature flag to immediate rollback.
   - We recommend a short cooldown and circuit-breaker at each step (10–30 minutes) before progressing.

3) KMS: yes, we support customer-managed AWS KMS keys and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. We'll coordinate a key policy and limited IAM role for Redwood's serving nodes.

Attachment: canary_runbook.xlsx (detailed gate triggers, contact escalation matrix)

I've attached a Phase-hours estimate: Phase0 40h, Phase1 120h, Phase2 60h, Phase3 24h. These are initial estimates to feed procurement SOW; Aditya can refine.

Also proposing a short cadence:
- Alignment call Thurs 06/26, 10am PT
- Deliver final SOW draft by 07/02

Cheers,
Ava

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@astra.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@astra.com
Date: 2026-06-26T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation timeline, feature-flag canaries, and telemetry handoff - Astra Financial

Hi Samantha and team — adding technical detail from the solutions side. Key notes:

- Integration steps (order):
  1) Network allowlist + quick smoke with a sandbox token
  2) Schema handshake (we validate field-level mappings and tokenization expectations)
  3) Auth verification (mutual TLS or token exchange)
  4) Small-volume end-to-end test with redacted payloads
  5) Canary ramp as described by Ava

- Telemetry specifics: we ship metrics over encrypted channel (TLS 1.2+). For metrics ingestion we recommend posting to a preconfigured endpoint in your monitoring stack (Datadog preferred) and Mirroring to Redwood's secure metrics store for troubleshooting (anonymized). We'll provide a mapping table that aligns our metric names to your existing observability taxonomy.

- Feature flags & gating: we integrate with your FF service (we've done LaunchDarkly, Split). If you prefer, Redwood can host short-lived feature flags for the canary window — but we recommend using Astra's flag service for final control.

- Rollback mechanics: our serving runtime supports immediate traffic split reversal (<30s) and session affinity cleanup; however, user-visible sessions may require short-timeout handling on your side to avoid duplicated requests.

I'll attach a short checklist in the shared drive. Happy to walk through this on the call.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: telemetry_schema.yaml (field-level metrics & example payload)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@astra.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@astra.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation timeline, feature-flag canaries, and telemetry handoff - Astra Financial

Ava/Aditya — this is helpful. A couple of final items before we lock calendar: 

- Procurement wants the phase-hour estimates broken down by deliverable (integration, testing, runbook). Can you provide a short table?
- Our security team asks that any sample payloads be hashed and redacted at rest; can you confirm you will not persist raw PII in your logs?
- We have an internal SLA requirement for max token latency at 95th <= 450ms once in steady state. Can Redwood commit to ops runbooks to meet this?

If all good, we can proceed to signature and target a soft go-live window of 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-18.

Thanks,
Samantha

Thanks Samantha — short answers and next steps: 

- Phase-hour breakdown:
  • Phase0 (Prework): 40h — network + key exchange + test data prep
  • Phase1 (Integration): 120h — connectors, schema validation, auth
  • Phase2 (Canary + Telemetry): 60h — runbook execution, telemetry baseline, monitoring tuning
  • Phase3 (Scale & Cutover): 24h — scale verification and SLA handoff
  (Total estimated engineering hours: 244h)

- PII handling: Redwood will only ingest hashed/redacted payloads for any sample collections. We will not persist raw PII in logs; policies and retention windows are in the attached PDF.

- SLA: we will commit to working-runbooks and a performance remediation plan; steady-state 95th latency target will be operated against our Dedicated SLA. We will include service credits in the SOW for missed latency SLOs per negotiated contract.

Next steps:
- I'll update the SOW and return by 07/02 with the phase-hour table included.
- I'll also send a DocuSign link for the SOW once procurement confirms billing milestones.
- Alignment call remains Thursday 06/26 10am PT (please confirm attendees).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — excited to get this started.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
